counterevidence_considered.description: The only subtraction-from-one construct in the workflow is (1 - agreement_flag) inside concordance_credit; I checked whether this could constitute complementation of the panel. It complements the boolean agreement flag to weight the mismatch credit (which is 0), not the panel value itself, so it cannot produce a complemented-panel comparison.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: (1 - agreement_flag) applies to the agreement flag, not to panel_allele; MISMATCH_CREDIT = 0

evidence.description: panel_state returns the staged panel_allele value unmodified (no subtraction from 1, no recoding), and concordance_credit compares the observed pcr_call directly against that supplied-coding value.

Independent recount from inputs/data.csv: pcr_call equals panel_allele as staged for 19 of 24 isolates (mismatches at ISO-004, ISO-007, ISO-013, ISO-018, ISO-023), matching the reported 19 agreeing units, rate 0.791667 (19/24), and emission 19.000 credits.

source_refs.quoted_text: Units whose pcr_call equals the staged panel_allele: 19

Per-unit agreement rate used in the emission accumulation: 0.791667 (19/24)
Accumulated concordance emission: 19.000 credits

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by searching the workflow for any transformation of the panel column before comparison: panel_state returns the raw staged string, and the comparison is a direct equality against the raw observed string (both columns stage only the tokens '0' and '1', so string equality is exact here). The only '1 - x' expression operates on the agreement flag, not the panel value. I then recomputed the agreement count by hand from the 24 rows against panel_allele as staged and obtained 19/24 with mismatches at ISO-004/007/013/018/023, exactly matching the reported rate and emission; a complemented-panel computation would instead have yielded 5/24 and 5.000 credits, which appear nowhere in this report. The falsification failed, so the no-issue verdict stands.
